claims.text: Enhanced short-range ordering in high-entropy nanoalloys reduces atomic mobility.
Reduced atomic mobility retards phase segregation at elevated temperatures.
Reduced atomic mobility retards grain coarsening at elevated temperatures.
High-entropy nanoalloys of identical overall composition can be prepared with different degrees of initial atomic short-range order.
Local short-range order is associated with atomic clustering patterns in high-entropy alloys.
High-temperature short-range ordering and chemical clustering occur in high-entropy alloys.
Pronounced short-range order provides entropic stabilization.
Entropic stabilization minimizes atomic diffusion pathways.
Enhanced initial short-range order preserves compositional homogeneity during high-temperature exposure.
Nanoalloys with enhanced initial short-range order will retain a more homogeneous single-phase structure than a minimally ordered baseline.
Enhanced initial short-range order will delay or reduce phase segregation relative to a minimally ordered baseline.
Enhanced initial short-range order will delay or reduce grain coarsening relative to a minimally ordered baseline.
An inert or vacuum environment prevents oxidation during the proposed high-temperature treatment.
The prediction applies from 900 to 1200 K for exposure durations up to 24 hours when oxidation and contamination are limited.
The degree of short-range order required for measurable stabilization depends on alloy composition.
Nanoscale interfacial effects influence the quantitative stability improvement associated with short-range order.
Tailored annealing protocols can selectively produce different initial short-range-order levels while otherwise preserving an identical nanoalloy comparison.
Comparable or greater segregation, grain coarsening, or compositional inhomogeneity in the enhanced-order samples would falsify the proposed stabilizing effect of short-range order.
